## Comparability note

Both companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) for FY2024, and both sets of figures come from their respective FY2024 Form 10-K filings [DOC-1], so the periods and accounting bases are directly comparable. No divestiture, spinoff, or segment-definition issue affects the comparison of these consolidated totals.

## (a) FY2024 operating margin

| | Operating revenue | Operating income | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| American Airlines Group | $54,211M [DOC-1] | $2,614M [DOC-1] | ≈ 4.8% |
| Southwest Airlines | $27,483M [DOC-1] | $321M [DOC-1] | ≈ 1.2% |

American: $2,614M ÷ $54,211M = 4.82%. Southwest: $321M ÷ $27,483M = 1.17%. **American leads on operating margin by roughly 3.7 percentage points** — its margin is about 4x Southwest's.

(Side note: Southwest's net income of $465M actually exceeds its operating income of $321M [DOC-1], implying net non-operating gains/interest income, whereas American's net income of $846M is well below its $2,614M operating income [DOC-1], consistent with a heavy interest burden on its debt load.)

## (b) Balance-sheet strength at Dec 31, 2024

| | Stockholders' equity (deficit) | Long-term debt | Debt / equity |
|---|---|---|---|
| American Airlines Group | –$3,977M [DOC-1] | $24,617M [DOC-1] | n/m (negative equity) |
| Southwest Airlines | $10,350M [DOC-1] | $6,697M [DOC-1] | 0.65x |

American ended FY2024 with a stockholders' **deficit** of $3,977M against $24,617M of long-term debt [DOC-1], so no meaningful leverage ratio can be computed — liabilities exceed assets. Southwest had $10,350M of positive equity and only $6,697M of long-term debt [DOC-1], a conservative 0.65x debt-to-equity. **Southwest leads decisively on balance-sheet strength**, with roughly 27% of American's long-term debt on a much smaller revenue base ($27.5B vs. $54.2B [DOC-1]).

## Does the same airline lead on both?

No. The comparison splits: American is the stronger operator on a margin basis in FY2024, while Southwest is far stronger on capital structure. American's superior margin is partly a byproduct of the leveraged model that produces its equity deficit, and its interest costs consume most of the operating income advantage (net income of $846M on $54.2B of revenue = 1.6% net margin, vs. Southwest's $465M on $27.5B = 1.7% [DOC-1]).

ANSWER: No — American leads on (a) FY2024 operating margin (4.8% vs. Southwest's 1.2%), while Southwest leads on (b) balance-sheet strength (+$10,350M equity and $6,697M long-term debt vs. American's –$3,977M equity deficit and $24,617M long-term debt).
